name: Ray Lackey

nadir.desc: The property consists of a primary residence with a dark roof and surrounding green lawn, along with a large detached outbuilding with a light-colored roof|A circular dirt and gravel driveway provides access from the road and loops through the site|Multiple vehicles are parked near the side building|Smaller structures are present on the property|Scattered trees and open dry terrain surround the developed area.

alpha.desc: The front portion of the property shows a large light-colored outbuilding with garage doors|A circular dirt and gravel driveway leads to the structure|Multiple vehicles are parked in the open area|The primary residence is partially visible to one side with green lawn|Scattered trees and dry open ground surround the buildings.

bravo.desc: The left side of the property shows the large light-colored outbuilding and a smaller shed behind it|Vehicles are parked nearby|Scattered trees and dry terrain extend around the structures|Portions of the primary residence roof are visible in the background.

charlie.desc: The rear area of the property shows the large light-colored outbuilding|The circular dirt and gravel driveway continues through the site|Multiple vehicles are present|A circular fire pit or similar feature is visible on the ground behind the side structure|Scattered trees and open dry land surround the area.

delta.desc: The right side of the property shows the primary residence with a covered porch area, the large light-colored outbuilding, and a smaller shed|Multiple vehicles are parked in the open dirt and gravel area|Scattered trees and dry terrain extend across the lot|The circular driveway provides access between the structures.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided by a long dirt and gravel driveway that leads from the road into a circular loop around the developed area. Multiple vehicles are parked near the large outbuilding. The primary residence has a green lawn perimeter. A large detached outbuilding with garage doors and a smaller shed are present on the property. Scattered trees and open dry terrain surround the buildings. The site is located in a rural residential area with neighboring homes on large lots and limited nearby development.
clarifications: Does the large outbuilding provide direct vehicle or pedestrian access into any interior space connected to the main house? Is the circular driveway fully passable for emergency vehicles in both directions? Are there any gates controlling access from the road onto the property? What is the primary use of the large outbuilding and the smaller shed? How much clear space exists around the main house given the surrounding trees and dry vegetation?
